'''Daniel Adzei Bekoe''' {{post nominals|post-noms=[[Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences|FGA]]|[[Pontifical Academy of Sciences|FPAS]]|[[World Academy of Sciences|FWAS]]}} (7 December 1928 – 5 September 2020) was a [[Ghanaian]] [[chemist]] and [[Academic staff|academic]]. He was Vice-Chancellor of the [[University of Ghana]] and also a former president of the [[Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences]].

==Early life and education==
Daniel Adzei Bekoe was born on 7 December 1928 to A.S. Adzete Bekoe and Jessie Nadu Bekoe (''née'' Awuletey) at [[Abokobi]]. His father was then a teacher at the Abokobi Presbyterian School. His father was transferred to teach at the Teshie Presbyterian School, Salem in 1934 and a year later, Daniel Bekoe began his early education at the school. He completed his early education in December 1942 and was enrolled at [[Achimota College]] in January 1943 after passing his Cambridge examinations. In 1947, he was a member of the first batch of students to be enrolled at Achimota for the newly introduced sixth form education. He entered the [[University of Ghana]], then the University College of the Gold Coast as one of the 92 students to be admitted as the first batch of students in the institution in 1948. He was also one of the first residents of the institution's first hall of residence; the Legon hall. In June, 1953 he graduated with First Class honours<ref>{{cite book |last=Amoak |first=Kwesi |date=1976 |title=Quest for excellence: biographies of 15 successful Ghanaians who passed through Legon |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=F54rAQAAIAAJ&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe |page=12|publisher=K. Amoak |isbn=9789988111830 }}</ref> receiving his University of&nbsp;London special degree in chemistry with subsidiary in Mathematics.<ref>{{cite book |last=Beeko |first=A. A. |date=2004 |title=The Trail Blazers: Fruits of the Presbyterian Church of Ghana, 1828-2003 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=onPZAAAAMAAJ&q=Adzete |page=144|publisher=Afram Publications (Ghana) |isbn=9789964703493}}</ref> He later received his PhD in Chemical Crystallography from the [[University of Oxford]] at [[Balliol College]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Proceedings of the Chemical Society |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uv86AAAAIAAJ&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe&pg=PA38 |publisher=Chemical Society (Great Britain) |page=20 |date=1955}}</ref><ref name="BEKOE">{{cite web |url=http://ieagh.org/professor-daniel-adzei-bekoe/ |title=Professor Daniel Adzei Bekoe |work=IEA Ghana |publisher=the Institute of Economic Affairs |access-date=16 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416144004/http://ieagh.org/professor-daniel-adzei-bekoe/ |archive-date=16 April 2019 |url-status=live|date=2014-06-27 }}</ref><ref name= "D. A. BEKOE">{{cite book |author=American Association for the Advancement of Science. |date=2013 |title=Science in Africa: setting research priorities: a symposium organized by the AAAS Sub-Saharan Africa Program, AAAS Annual Meeting, Chicago, Illinois, February 10, 1992 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZPxDAQAAIAAJ&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe |page=61}}</ref>

==Career==
He was appointed lecturer of the [[University of Ghana]] in 1958. As a lecturer of the University of Ghana, he rose through the ranks to become a senior lecturer and later, professor of chemistry in 1974. While at the university he was appointed master of Legon hall.<ref>{{cite book |last=Daniel |first=Ebow |date=1999 |title=Mr. Registrar : the making of an amanuensis |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JOwsAQAAIAAJ&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe |page=78|publisher=Woeli Pub. Services |isbn=9789964978594 }}</ref> From 1971 to 1973, he was dean of the faculty of science at the university. He was appointed pro vice chancellor in 1973 and vice chancellor of the university from 1976 to 1983.<ref>{{cite book |last=Acheampong |first=I. K. |date=1976 |title=Fourth Year in Office of Colonel Ignatius Kutu Acheampong: 13th January 1975-12th January 1976 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5XUNAQAAIAAJ&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe |page=27}}</ref> He spent various periods at the [[University of Ibadan]], [[Nigeria]] and also at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] as an advanced research scholar.<ref>{{cite journal |title=International educational exchange and related exchange-of-persons activities for African countries south of the Sahara, Volume 3 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uv86AAAAIAAJ&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe&pg=PA38 |publisher=United States. Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs |page=38 |date=1959}}</ref> In 1980, he was appointed president of the [[International Council of Scientific Unions]] (ICSU).<ref>{{cite book |last=Addy |first=M. A. |authorlink=Marian Ewurama Addy |date=2011 |title=Rewards : an autobiography |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9gpkHOFb5DwC&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe&pg=PA320 |page=285|publisher=African Books Collective |isbn=9789988037826 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1= Dooge |first1=J. C. I. |last2=Brennan |first2=Maureen |last3=Goodman |first3=G. T. |last4=La Rivière |first4=J. W. |last5=Marton-Lefèvre |first5=J. | first6=T. |last6=O'Riordan |date=1992 |title=An Agenda of Science for Environment and development into the 21st century: based on a conference held in Vienna, Austria, 1991 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XAAiqgNXIcEC&q=d+a+bekoe&pg=PA315 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |page=315|isbn=9780521437615}}</ref> On 26 September 1983 he was elected as a member of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{cite book |last1= Chagas |first1=C. |last2=Pullman |first2=B. |date=1984 |title=Specificity in Biological Interactions: Proceedings of a Working Group at the Pontifical Academy of Sciences November 9–11, 1983 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IF39CAAAQBAJ&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe&pg=PR24 |publisher=Dordrecht Springer Netherlands |page=24|isbn=9789400964570}}</ref> that same year he became a founding fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.twas-rossa.org.za/network/item/1-twas-fellows/14-bekoe-daniel-adzei |title=Daniel Adzei Bekoe |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences- Regional Office of sub-Saharan Africa |access-date=16 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416144003/https://www.twas-rossa.org.za/network/item/1-twas-fellows/14-bekoe-daniel-adzei |archive-date=16 April 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> He joined [[UNESCO]] Regional Office of Science and Technology for Africa in [[Nairobi]], [[Kenya]] as its director. In October 1983 he was the UNESCO Representative to [[Kenya]], [[Mauritius]], [[Seychelles]], [[Somalia]], [[Tanzania]] and [[Uganda]], he served in this capacity until December, 1985.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://unescoghana.org/achievements/ |title=GHANA'S CONTRIBUTION TO UNESCO'S WORK |publisher=UNESCO GHANA |access-date=16 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901021951/http://unescoghana.org/achievements/ |archive-date=1 September 2018 |url-status=live|date=2017-05-26 }}</ref> In January 1986, he became the Regional Director for Eastern and Southern Africa, International Development Research Centre of Canada in Nairobi, Kenya until his retirement in March 1992. From 1978 to 1982 he served on the Council of the [[United Nations University]], [[Tokyo]], Japan.<ref name= "D. A. BEKOE"/> From 1993 to 1996 he was president of the [[Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. In 2003, he played an instrumental role in the founding of the [[Presbyterian University College]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Beeko |first=A. A. |date=2006 |title=The impact of the traditions of the Presbyterian Church of Ghana on the development of contemporary Ghanaian society: date, 19th-21st October, 2005, venue, Osu Ebenezer Presbyterian Church Hall |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=T24mAQAAIAAJ&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe |page=43}}</ref> He was a member and subsequently chairman of the [[Council of State (Ghana)|Council of State]] from 2005 to 2008<ref>GNA,[https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Adzei-Bekoe-elected-Chairman-of-Council-of-State-77989 "Adzei Bekoe elected Chairman of Council of State"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416144003/https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Adzei-Bekoe-elected-Chairman-of-Council-of-State-77989 |date=2019-04-16 }}, Ghanaweb, 24 March 2005.</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Boadu-Ayeboafoh |first=Yaw |date=2006-10-20 |title=Adja Takpor has paid his due |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_leTZ5s6v24C&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe&pg=PA3 |work=Daily Graphic |access-date=2019-04-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |author=Sage Reference |date=2013 |title=Worldwide government directory, with inter-governmental organizations : nations, intergovernmental organizations. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CQWhAQAAQBAJ&q=daniel+adzei+bekoe&pg=PA643 |page=643|publisher=CQ Press |isbn=9781452299372 }}</ref> and also chairman of the [[Ghana Atomic Energy Commission]] (GAEC).<ref>GNA,[https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Nuclear-power-is-long-term-Adzei-Bekoe-122575 "Nuclear power is long term - Adzei Bekoe"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416144004/https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Nuclear-power-is-long-term-Adzei-Bekoe-122575 |date=2019-04-16 }}, Ghanaweb, 17 April 2007.</ref> He was also a member of the [[The&nbsp;Institute&nbsp;of&nbsp;Economic&nbsp;Affairs,&nbsp;Ghana|Institute&nbsp;of&nbsp;Economic&nbsp;Affairs]] board of directors.<ref name="BEKOE"/>

== Death ==
Daniel Adzei Bekoe died in Accra on 5 September 2020, aged 91.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Notice of Death - Professor Daniel Adzei Bekoe, former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ghana {{!}} University of Ghana|url=https://www.ug.edu.gh/news/notice-death-professor-daniel-adzei-bekoe-former-vice-chancellor-university-ghana|access-date=2020-10-20|website=www.ug.edu.gh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Notice of Death - Professor Daniel Adzei Bekoe, former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ghana {{!}} UG Alumni Association|url=https://alumni.ug.edu.gh/node/364|access-date=2020-10-20|website=alumni.ug.edu.gh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-09-19|title=Former UG Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Daniel Adzei Bekoe, passes on|url=https://www.universnewsroom.com/news/former-ug-vice-chancellor-prof-daniel-adzei-bekoe-passes-on/|access-date=2020-10-20|website=Radio Univers 105.7FM|language=en}}</ref>

== Publications ==
Source:<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.accademiascienze.va/content/accademia/en/academicians/ordinary/bekoe.html |title=Daniel Adzei Bekoe |publisher=the Pontifical Academy of Sciences |access-date=16 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416144006/http://www.accademiascienze.va/content/accademia/en/academicians/ordinary/bekoe.html |archive-date=16 April 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>
* ''The Crystal Structure of i-Erythritol and its relationships to some derived d and 1 and racemic substances'' (with Powell, H.M.),&nbsp;Proceedings of the Royal Society, 250 A, pp.&nbsp;301–15 (1959);
* ''The Crystal Structure of Tetracyanoethylene'' (with Trueblood, K.N.),&nbsp;Zeitschrift für Krystallographie, 113, pp.&nbsp;1–22 (1960);
* ''The Crystal Structure of the Hexahydrated Calcium Salt of Hexacyanoisobutylene'' (with Gantzel, P.K. and Trueblood, K.N.),&nbsp;Acta Crystallographica, 22, pp.&nbsp;657–665 (1967);
* ''A Re-investigation of the Crystal Structure of Tetracyanoethylene'' (with Trueblood, K.N.), Abstracts of Bozeman Meeting of the American Crystallographic Association, p.&nbsp;87 (1964);
* ''Molecular Structure of Cedrela Odorata Substance B'' (with Adeoye, S.A.), Chemical Communications, 14, pp.&nbsp;301–2 (1965);
* ''The Crystallographic Evidence for the Molecular Structure of Mexicanolide'', PhD Thesis of S.A. Adeoye (1967);
* ''The Crystal Structure of N, N-Diethyldithiocarbamato-triphenylstanne'', MSc Thesis of K.A. Woode (1975);
* ''Hexamethylbenzene-Tetracyamoethylene (1:1) Complex at 113K: Structure and Energy Calculations'' (with Maverick, E. and Trueblood, K.N.),&nbsp;Acta Crystallographica, B 34, pp.&nbsp;2777–2781 (1978);
* ''The Dilemma of the Scientist (Contribution to a Symposium on 'Building an Intellectual Community in Ghana''', Proceedings of the Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences) (1970), pp.&nbsp;61–4;
* ''The Energy Problem in Perspective'',&nbsp;Proceedings of the Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences, XIV, pp.&nbsp;15–24 (1976);
* ''International Cooperation in Science and Technology for Development Statement on the Symposium'',&nbsp;International Symposium on Science and Technology for Development, Singapore, 22–26 January 1979, pp.&nbsp;7–13;
* ''Mobilizing Science and Technology to Increase Endogenous Capabilities in Developing Countries,&nbsp;Science, Technology and Society – Needs, Challenges and Limitations''&nbsp;(K.H. Standke and M. Anandakrishna, eds.), Pergamon Press (1980), pp.&nbsp;457–63.

==Honours==
The Central Science Laboratory of the [[University of Ghana]] was named in his honour.<ref>GNA,[https://www.newsghana.com.gh/ug-to-continue-naming-her-buildings-after-distinguished-personalities/ "UG To Continue Naming Her Buildings After Distinguished Personalities"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416144006/https://www.newsghana.com.gh/ug-to-continue-naming-her-buildings-after-distinguished-personalities/ |date=2019-04-16 }}, News Ghana, 12 November 2013.</ref> He received an honorary D.Sc. from the [[University of Ghana]].<ref name="BEKOE"/><ref name= "D. A. BEKOE"/>
